2.content:
This SOW covers the Silicon COT Supply Chain implementation for GOOGLE, using a baseline-template approach to standardize core Order-to-Cash processes, address approved localization needs, and deliver the solution across onsite and offshore teams over the agreed 18-month term.

- Establish a global design for Silicon COT Supply Chain processes using industry best practices, fit-to-standard workshops, and stakeholder sign-off.
- Deliver the implementation through defined stages including blueprinting and design, integration and data activities, sprint-based build, testing, training, and hypercare.
- Drive sustained adoption and value realization through organizational change management, user adoption support, and continuous enhancement planning.

Deferred scope decisions, project dependencies, and other engagement assumptions are set out in Section 10 (Key Assumptions) and Section 21 (Key Observations).

3.1.content: GOOGLE is undertaking the Silicon COT Supply Chain implementation to establish a standardized global design for core Order-to-Cash and supply chain processes while addressing approved localization requirements across plants, legal entities, and partner operations. The current landscape requires clearer definition of the AS-IS baseline across foundry and OSAT operations, including purchase order flows, subcontracting settlement, batch and lot traceability, full genealogy tracking, enterprise structure, and master data readiness. Key pain points include gaps in current organizational setup for the COT model, fragmented integration patterns across E2Open, Kinaxis, and SAP S/4HANA, uneven visibility into data flows and message structures, and the need to align business process design with technical mappings and execution planning. The business drivers for this engagement are to create a scalable global template, improve traceability and supply collaboration, strengthen cost and yield visibility, and support a controlled deployment model with stakeholder sign-off.

3.2.content:
- Establish an agreed AS-IS baseline across front-end and back-end Silicon supply chain processes.
- Define a global TO-BE process and organizational design for the Silicon BU using a baseline-template approach.
- Standardize core processes while incorporating approved local and site-specific requirements.
- Define end-to-end data flows, integration requirements, and system boundaries across SAP S/4HANA, E2Open, and Kinaxis.
- Confirm master data, transactional data, and reporting requirements needed for the COT operating model.
- Develop a sprint-based execution plan with clear scope, priorities, dependencies, milestones, and ownership.
- Validate the design through stakeholder workshops, playback sessions, and formal sign-off.

3.3.content:
The target state is a standardized Silicon supply chain model in which planning, procurement, subcontracting, traceability, and reporting operate through a governed global template with approved local variations. Demand, supply, and collaboration signals flow through the defined planning and integration landscape, with SAP S/4HANA serving as the core transactional platform and E2Open and Kinaxis supporting agreed planning and partner collaboration use cases. The future-state process supports end-to-end lot genealogy from wafer through probe, die bank, assembly, test, and finished goods, with aligned enterprise structure, master data, and integration controls. Execution is expected to progress from AS-IS discovery to TO-BE blueprinting, technical mapping, and sprint-based delivery.

4.1.content: The engagement covers GOOGLE Silicon supply chain operations supporting TSMC, KYEC, and SPIL in Taiwan, together with GOOGLE Hub and warehouse operations in North America. Delivery will be executed through a blended onsite and offshore model, with onsite activities aligned to North America and offshore delivery supporting build, integration, and testing activities. Any additional region, plant, warehouse, or partner location not expressly listed in this SOW is outside scope unless added through the Change Management Process.

4.2.content: In-scope business processes cover the Customer Owned Tooling (COT) supply chain model for the Silicon business unit, including constrained supply planning with yield, purchase order and forecast collaboration, commit visibility, subcontracting-related planning flows, material and inventory planning, batch and lot traceability, and end-to-end genealogy across wafer, probe, die bank, assembly, test, and finished goods. The scope also includes AS-IS discovery, fit-gap assessment, TO-BE process design, and validation of process flows needed to support the target global template and approved localization requirements.

4.3.content: Technical scope includes solution design, configuration, and integration activities across SAP S/4HANA, Kinaxis, E2Open, and agreed connected systems within the Silicon COT landscape. In-scope work includes use of the existing integration framework currently used for machines planning, adaptation of the existing data template for Silicon planning requirements, delta integration design and build using BTP-IS, and technical mapping for inbound and outbound data flows needed for planning, execution, traceability, and analytics. Resource master, yield, unit-of-measure, capacity, contract manufacturer, demand, WIP, wafer plan, and agreed master and transactional data integrations are in scope. Any net-new interface pattern or system not listed in Section 4.6 requires confirmation through discovery and, if needed, formal change control.

4.4.content: Services included in this engagement are project management, fit-gap analysis, AS-IS discovery, TO-BE process design, business process design documentation, functional specifications for approved custom development, configuration and build, test planning and execution, unit testing, system integration testing, regression testing, performance testing, train-the-trainer activities, user acceptance testing support, data migration support, cutover planning and execution, hypercare, organizational change management, and knowledge transfer to the support team. Delivery will follow a phased agile model across Explore, Build, and Deploy.

4.5.content: Application scope includes Kinaxis, SAP S/4HANA, and E2Open for the Silicon business unit. Within Kinaxis, the scope covers supply planning, constraint planning, inventory planning, analytics and reporting, and data integration. Within SAP S/4HANA, the scope covers Production Planning and Materials Management, together with process integration required to support the end-to-end COT model. Controlling-related inputs and activities required for the target operating model will be provided and staffed by GOOGLE. Application functionality outside these named areas is excluded unless expressly added through approved change control.

5.content:
The solution architecture will use SAP S/4HANA as the transactional and execution backbone, Kinaxis as the planning orchestration layer, and E2Open as the supplier-collaboration platform for foundry and OSAT interactions. The architecture will support closed-loop planning and execution across demand, supply, subcontracting, traceability, and reporting processes for the Silicon COT model.

Integration design will reuse GOOGLE’s existing planning framework where applicable, extend agreed data templates for Silicon planning requirements, and implement approved delta interfaces through SAP BTP Integration Suite. Data flows will cover agreed master and transactional objects across SAP S/4HANA, Kinaxis, E2Open, PLM, and the reporting landscape, with lot-level collaboration boundaries maintained through E2Open and unit-level test boundary integration limited to agreed reporting and execution needs.

<IMAGE id="689305094e2e"/>

The deployment model is a phased implementation delivered through Explore, Build, and Deploy, with MVP execution planned in two phases and a third scaling phase for broader adoption. Delivery will follow a blended onsite and offshore model, with North America-based onsite governance and stakeholder alignment supported by offshore build, integration, testing, and release activities.

Change governance will be managed through a baseline-template approach that prioritizes business process design before configuration, fit-to-standard decision-making, stakeholder sign-off on the global design, and controlled incorporation of approved localization requirements. Governance will track milestones, risks, dependencies, and cross-functional decisions across GOOGLE, foundry, and OSAT stakeholders, with any scope, interface, or design expansion handled through the Change Management Process defined in Section 17.

6.1.content:
Delivery will follow a phased agile model across Prepare, Explore, Realize, and Deploy, aligned to the approved Explore, Build, and Deploy structure for this engagement.

- **Prepare:** finalize project plan and charter, mobilize teams, confirm governance, and align scope, dependencies, and readiness.
- **Explore:** complete AS-IS discovery, fit-gap assessment, business scenario mapping, localization validation, design reviews, and sign-off of the global solution baseline.
- **Realize:** execute baseline configuration, approved custom development, integration mapping and build, mock data loads, unit testing, sprint-based configuration, reports and dashboards, and train-the-trainer activities.
- **Deploy:** complete SIT, UAT support, regression and performance testing, cutover planning, go/no-go governance, end-user training support, go-live, hypercare, knowledge transfer, and project closure.

The rollout will progress in three phases: Phase 1 to enable TSMC purchase order capability, Phase 2 to deliver the core MVP for wafer-to-finished-goods planning, and Phase 3 to extend additional finished goods and broader adoption scope.

**Implementation / rollout diagram:** Prepare → Explore → Realize → Deploy; Release sequence: Phase 1 → Phase 2 MVP → Phase 3 scale-out.

7.1.content:
Project governance will operate through a tiered model covering executive oversight, delivery management, and cross-functional working teams. Executive sponsors from GOOGLE and Bristlecone will review milestone readiness, major risks, scope-impacting decisions, and release go/no-go items. The Program Manager will run day-to-day governance, maintain the integrated plan, track risks, dependencies, and decisions, and coordinate functional, integration, data, testing, and change activities across onsite and offshore teams.

Working-level governance will include regular design, integration, and release-planning forums during Explore, Realize, and Deploy. Issues will be escalated first to the Program Manager, then to the solution and business leads for resolution, and then to the executive sponsors where timeline, budget, scope, or policy decisions are required. Any change affecting agreed scope, timeline, commercials, interfaces, or localization requirements will be routed through the Change Management Process in Section 17.

22.content: The recommendations in this section are intended to tighten governance, preserve scope control, and align acceptance with release readiness across the 18-month implementation term. Priority should be given to baselining the delivery matrix, freezing deferred Phase 3 decisions before downstream build planning, and enforcing change control for any interface, localization, partner, or release-scope expansion. Acceptance should remain tied to objective deliverable and test-exit criteria, named sign-off owners, and documented defect disposition before release approval.

22.1.content:
- Baseline a Milestone Deliverables Matrix aligned to Sections 6, 9, and 11, with owners, due dates, review windows, and sign-off points for each phase and release.
- Freeze Phase 3 rollout scope, region coverage, and partner-onboarding boundaries before detailed planning for that release begins.
- Maintain a single decision and dependency log covering design, integration, data, localization, security-role, and environment-readiness items.
- Route any increase in interface count, custom development, localization scope, partner onboarding, or release content through the Change Management Process in Section 17.
- Confirm governance cadence for executive reviews, working-team reviews, test-status reviews, and go/no-go checkpoints during mobilization.
- Track connected-system dependencies across SAP S/4HANA, Kinaxis, E2Open, PLM, MES/Test Hub, BigQuery, and SAP BTP-IS with named owners and escalation paths.
- Confirm the RACI used for execution is the approved project RACI and reflects the roles defined in Section 7.2.
- Review commercial and schedule impact promptly when assumptions on client participation, data readiness, access, or localization validation do not hold.

22.2.content:
- Keep acceptance at the deliverable and release level, not only at the phase level, with measurable criteria, review timelines, and named approvers.
- Require approved test plans, scripts, and exit criteria before SIT and UAT execution begins for each release.
- Do not advance a release with open Sev 1 defects; allow open Sev 2 defects only with documented workaround or approved disposition.
- Ensure design sign-off is completed before configuration or custom development proceeds beyond the approved baseline.
- Validate integration and data outputs against agreed source-to-target rules, not narrative confirmation alone.
- Confirm training completion, cutover readiness, and hypercare exit through documented evidence, attendance, and closure criteria.
- Record all sign-offs, defects, deferrals, and go/no-go decisions in the project governance record for auditability.
